  "text": "The constable drew his truncheon, though there was nowhere on the stairs to strike. Ada held the letter against her palm. It was cold and heavier than wood ought to be.

“Put it back,” Venn said. “The others are moving.”

Five letters dragged themselves across the boards. They stopped at the edge of the water, facing the one in Ada’s hand.

A wet shoe appeared on the lowest visible stair. Then another. Above them hung the hem of Mara’s blue coat, dripping steadily onto dry wood. Ada could see no face beneath its hood.

“What was carved beneath her name?” Ada asked again.

The coat swayed. “A date.”

“No,” said the constable. He sounded surprised to hear himself speak. “I saw it when we brought her in. It was a name.”

Venn looked at him. “Whose?”

The constable’s key fell from his belt. It struck a stair and vanished into the water without a sound.

“My daughter’s,” he said.

The hood lifted. From within came a small voice: “May I leave?”

Ada closed her fist around the letter. The warning had said not to answer until it asked. It had not said they must answer then.

Behind the coat, the front door swung open. Rain shone on the street beyond, and for one moment Ada saw a child standing there with her back to the house.

The constable started down. Ada caught his sleeve.

“Is that your daughter?” she asked.

He stared at the child. “I don’t know.”

The water withdrew one step. Beneath it, freshly cut into the stair, was his name."
